title: Spike: Salsa incremental computation (boundary-finding)
description:
Lighter-weight evaluation. Does Salsa fill a distinct role (fine-grained per-file query memoization) or is it redundant with differential dataflow? Model Sutra's query hierarchy as Salsa queries, prototype parse-to-outline pipeline, test cross-file queries, compare with differential dataflow results.

This is a boundary-finding exercise: adopt / complement (with boundary defined) / skip.

acceptance_criteria.text: Salsa query graph modeled for Sutra's core tools
Parse-to-outline pipeline with incremental updates working
Comparison matrix against differential dataflow written

execution_record: Salsa 0.26 spike on sutra (74 files). Single-file memoization: 9600x warm speedup, but cross-file aggregation (symbol index, ref resolution) recomputes fully when any file changes — same bottleneck as current approach. DD handles this better (tuple-level incrementality). Salsa adds 19 crate deps for marginal gain over SQLite+content-hash. Verdict: skip. See docs/v1-spikes/salsa.md.
